candidates.title: Pranos Fusion — Company Website
candidates.notes: Accessible HTML (not JS-blocked). Confirms Jenga as 'tokamak design and plasma-control software' that 'integrates control-oriented design from the outset'. Critically, states JENGA and PRAGYA are 'engineered to integrate HTS magnet modules' — first public confirmation of HTS magnet route. No simulation outputs or validated model results published. Also documents MAGGA as HTS magnet sub-program.

candidates.title: Pranos Nets $6.8 Mn To Build Tokamak, Superconducting Magnets For Nuclear Fusion — inc42
candidates.notes: Full article content accessible. Documents $6.8M Series A round (March 24, 2026), lead investors pi Ventures and Ankur Capital, with participation from Industrial47, Lalit Keshre (Groww co-founder), Razorpay founders, Bhukhanwala Industries. Describes three-part stack: JENGA (design/control software), PRAGYA (tokamak platform), MAGGA (HTS magnet program). States JENGA is 'likely to convert into a revenue making product soon' with 'pilot level integration expected within a year'. First tokamak commissioning targeted for 2026. Significant update to analysis — prior funding was $417K seed; now $6.8M total.

candidates.notes: Same funding round covered in inc42 article. Describes Pranos as 'high-field fusion reactor technology'. Confirms MAGGA HTS magnet program. No additional technical content beyond inc42 article; skipped extraction to preserve budget.

Documents $6.8M funding round (March 24, 2026). Significant update to analysis funding section. Provides clearest public description of Jenga as plasma-control software (not just simulation/digital twin). No model outputs.

gaps_attempted.notes: No published Jenga simulation outputs or digital twin validation results found across all searches. G-14 remains open. The Jenga platform is now better characterized as 'design and plasma-control software' (not solely a digital twin) — the IAEA FUSE profile's description of MHD/transport/neutronics/thermal-structural modules appears to be aspirational rather than validated. Two high-value ancillary sources were extracted: (1) company website confirming HTS magnet route via MAGGA program; (2) $6.8M funding round article (March 2026) with product stack detail. These address other analysis gaps (G-3 magnet type, funding accuracy) even though G-14 (Jenga validation outputs) remains unresolved.

key_incidental_findings: Pranos confirmed HTS magnet route via MAGGA program — website states PRAGYA and JENGA are 'engineered to integrate HTS magnet modules'. Partially resolves G-3.
Major funding update: $6.8M Series A closed March 24, 2026 (led by pi Ventures and Ankur Capital). Analysis currently shows only $417K seed round — significant staleness.

Jenga characterized as 'plasma-control software' for design-to-machine integration, not purely a physics simulation platform. The integrated simulation scope described in IAEA FUSE (MHD, transport, neutronics, etc.) may reflect aspirational scope rather than currently validated capabilities.
First tokamak (PRAGYA) commissioning targeted for 2026 per funding announcement.
MAGGA is the explicit name for Pranos's HTS magnet sub-program.
